qt: to the Commission Mounir Satouri (Verts/ALE), Caroline Roose (Verts/ALE) Subject:

The Outlaw Ocean Project journalist organisation has brought to light that, despite UN bans, predominantly North Korean women working in seafood processing plants in China are being subjected to forced labour, violence, sexual assault and captivity. Dalian Haiqing Food is one of the companies accused in the investigation. This company supplied foodstuffs to the Belgian firm Pittman Seafoods, which in turn supplies the Compass Group. The European Parliament has conducted an investigation and stated that it is ‘confident that there is no link between the abovementioned company and Parliament’s supply by its contractor’. Dalian Haiqing Food is one of the suppliers of Sysco France, which supplied the Commission’s canteens in 2022 and 2023. 1.
Has an investigation into using Sysco France as a supplier also been conducted by the Commission? If so, what are its findings?

The Outlaw Ocean Project has shown that forced labour exists and that it is difficult to trace. Supply chains can be opaque. What lines of accountability and monitoring tools has the Commission put in place to guarantee the reliability of suppliers?
at: (English version) to the Commission Mounir Satouri (Verts/ALE), Caroline Roose (Verts/ALE) (4 March 2024) Subject: Accusations of forced labour levelled against companies supplying seafood to the European institutions The Outlaw Ocean Project journalist organisation has brought to light that, despite UN bans, predominantly North Korean women working in seafood processing plants in China are being subjected to forced labour, violence, sexual assault and captivity. Dalian Haiqing Food is one of the companies accused in the investigation. This company supplied foodstuffs to the Belgian firm Pittman Seafoods, which in turn supplies the Compass Group. The European Parliament has conducted an investigation and stated that it is ‘confident that there is no link between the above-mentioned company and Parliament’s supply by its contractor’. Dalian Haiqing Food is one of the suppliers of Sysco France, which supplied the Commission’s canteens in 2022 and 2023. 1. Has an investigation into using Sysco France as a supplier also been conducted by the Commission? If so, what are its findings? 2. The Outlaw Ocean Project has shown that forced labour exists and that it is difficult to trace. Supply chains can be opaque. What lines of accountability and monitoring tools has the Commission put in place to guarantee the reliability of suppliers? (20 June 2024) Following these serious accusations, the Commission requested its services in charge of catering in Brussels and in Luxembourg, which are currently supplied by Sysco, to check these allegations. Sysco confirmed that it no longer sources, directly or indirectly, from Dalian Haiqing Food. Regarding the accountability and monitoring tools to guarantee the reliability of suppliers, the Commission catering services require their suppliers to sign a declaration on the non-existence of exclusion grounds and the fulfilment of the selection criteria. The catering services systematically check potential suppliers against the EDES list (1). In addition, they require a Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) sustainable fishing certificate from their suppliers. More generally, in 2022, the Commission adopted a proposal for a directive on corporate sustainability due diligence (2) to foster sustainable and responsible corporate behaviour. The directive will require large companies to identify, mitigate and bring to an end adverse human rights and labour rights impacts throughout their chains of activities, including in relation to forced labour. Fines can be imposed on companies for non-compliance. The Commission also proposed in 2022 a regulation on prohibiting products made with forced labour on the EU market (3). If during the investigation the competent authorities find that the products concerned have been made with forced labour, they will prohibit the making available of those products and order the withdrawal and the disposal of those already made available on the EU market. The European Parliament and the Council reached agreement on the two legislative proposals in 2024.
